evidence: Varr. RR 1.7.1: ager spectat ad merīdiānam caelī partem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First “of midday” (merīdiānus somnus, the siesta), and so of the south, where the sun stands at noon (see south). Facing south is in merīdiem spectāre (Cato, below).

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.50: aquilōnia tum austrālis; Tusc. 1.68: austrālis ōra (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From auster, the south wind (see south wind); Cicero’s word for the southern regions of the earth.

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg.; also Plin.
terms.comment: As a noun, austrīna are the southern parts of a country (Pliny).
Late (Lactantius, Firmicus); Traupman uses it, but merīdiānus is the classical word.

phrases.latin: sī poteris, sub rādīce montis siet, in merīdiem spectet, locō salūbrī
phrases.english: if you can, let it lie at the foot of a mountain, facing south, in a healthy spot

phrases.latin: ager spectat ad merīdiānam caelī partem
phrases.english: the land faces the southern quarter of the sky

sources: Lewis & Short: meridianus · Lewis & Short: australis · Lewis & Short: austrinus · Lewis & Short: meridionalis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 85, 206, 383.
